```{python}
adata = sc.read(path_adata)

# UMAP for the plots, set by --umap_for_plots (default X_umap_scvi, the graph clustering uses).
# X_umap_pca is the PCA-based UMAP; X_umap is a copy kept for tools such as sc.pl.umap, and older
# outputs may only have X_umap.
from IPython.display import display, HTML

def resolve_umap(adata, requested):
    requested = str(requested).strip() if requested else ""
    for key in ([requested, f"X_{requested}"] if requested else []):
        if key in adata.obsm:
            return key, None
    for key in ["X_umap_scvi", "X_umap_pca", "X_umap"]:
        if key in adata.obsm:
            note = (f"UMAP '{requested}' was not found in adata.obsm, plotting '{key}' instead. "
                    f"Available: {', '.join(adata.obsm.keys())}.") if requested else None
            return key, note
    raise ValueError(f"No UMAP found in adata.obsm (available: {', '.join(adata.obsm.keys())})")

default_umap, umap_note = resolve_umap(adata, UMAP_FOR_PLOTS)
if umap_note:
    display(HTML(f"<p><b>Note:</b> {umap_note}</p>"))

pca_umap = "X_umap_pca" if "X_umap_pca" in adata.obsm else "X_umap"
# X_umap and X_umap_pca are the same (PCA-based) embedding
pca_umaps = ("X_umap", "X_umap_pca")
comparison_umaps = [(key, title) for key, title in [("X_umap_scvi", "scVI UMAP"), (pca_umap, "PCA UMAP")]
                    if key in adata.obsm and key != default_umap
                    and not (key in pca_umaps and default_umap in pca_umaps)]
```

## <font color='green'>Predicted labels</font>

Labels such as cell types are predicted for each cell by CellTypist (pre-trained logistic regression models, columns `celltypist:<model>`) and/or by scANVI reference mapping (columns `scanvi:<model>`). Predicted labels of the selected model(s) and the confidence of the predictions (columns ending in `:conf`) are displayed in the UMAPs below. Counts for the predicted labels are summarised in the table(s).

```{python}
# Reference models can predict hundreds of labels. Only the max_predicted_labels labels with the most
# cells are coloured, the others are grouped into one grey "other" category. Grouped columns are plotted
# from a small in-memory AnnData, so scanpy never writes to the report object.
import anndata as ad
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import display, HTML

# set by --report_max_celltype_labels (default 50); keeps the legend and the count table readable
max_predicted_labels = int(MAX_CELLTYPE_LABELS)

def group_predicted_labels(values, max_labels):
    # cells per label, most cells first; the labels after the first max_labels are grouped as "other"
    counts = values.value_counts()
    counts = counts[counts > 0]
    top, rest = counts.iloc[:max_labels], counts.iloc[max_labels:]
    return top, rest, f"other ({len(rest)} labels)"

def grouped_labels_note(top, rest):
    return (f"Showing the {len(top)} labels with the most cells out of {len(top) + len(rest)}; "
            f"the other {len(rest)} labels ({rest.sum()} cells)")

# obs column prefixes of the label prediction tools; their ':conf' columns are plotted as continuous values
prediction_prefixes = ('celltypist:', 'scanvi:')
predicted_labels = [ colname for colname in adata.obs.columns if colname.startswith(prediction_prefixes) ]
for label in predicted_labels:
    if label.endswith(':conf'):
        sc.pl.embedding(adata, basis=default_umap, color=label)
        continue

    top, rest, other_name = group_predicted_labels(adata.obs[label], max_predicted_labels)
    if rest.empty:
        sc.pl.embedding(adata, basis=default_umap, color=label)
        continue

    values = adata.obs[label].astype(object)
    grouped = values.where(values.isin(top.index) | values.isna(), other_name).to_numpy()
    # "other" cells first, so they are drawn below the coloured cells
    order = np.argsort(grouped != other_name, kind="stable")
    label_obs = pd.DataFrame({label: pd.Categorical(grouped[order], categories=[*top.index, other_name])},
                             index=adata.obs_names[order])
    adata_label = ad.AnnData(obs=label_obs, obsm={default_umap: np.asarray(adata.obsm[default_umap])[order]})

    # scanpy's default colours for this many categories (default_102), grey for "other"
    label_palette = dict(zip(top.index, sc.pl.palettes.default_102))
    label_palette[other_name] = "lightgrey"
    sc.pl.embedding(adata_label, basis=default_umap, color=label, palette=label_palette)
    display(HTML(f"<p><b>Note:</b> {grouped_labels_note(top, rest)} are shown in grey as 'other'.</p>"))
```

```{python}
from IPython.display import display, HTML
import base64

for label in predicted_labels:
    if not label.endswith(':conf'):
        html = f'<font color="black"><details><summary>Click to expand {label} table</summary>'
        top, rest, other_name = group_predicted_labels(adata.obs[label], max_predicted_labels)
        if rest.empty:
            df = adata.obs.value_counts(label).rename_axis(label).reset_index(name='number of cells')
        else:
            # top labels, then one row with the cells of all other labels
            df = pd.DataFrame({label: [*top.index, other_name], 'number of cells': [*top.to_numpy(), rest.sum()]})
            html += f"<p><b>Note:</b> {grouped_labels_note(top, rest)} are summed in the last row.</p>"
        html += '<div style="overflow-y: scroll; overflow-x: scroll; max-height: 400px">' + df.to_html() + '</div></details></font>'
        display(HTML(html))
```

```{python}
# overlap with annotation
import pandas as pd
import anndata as ann

def create_overlap_pct_label(adata: ann.AnnData, list_clusters: list, clustering: str, annotation: str, 
                             ntop: int=5, min_overlap_ratio: float=0.05) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Computes the overlap with a given annotation for each cluster

    Parameters
    ----------
    adata: ann.AnnData
        AnnData object containing the clusters and annotation labels
    list_clusters: list 
        A list of cluster IDs defining the order of rows in the output table
    clustering: str
        Name of clustering entry
    annotation: str
        Name of the annotation, e.g. celltypist annotation
    ntop: int
        Number of top annotations to be displayed
    min_overlap_ratio: float
        Minimum ration of cells to consider annotation label for output

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        Table listing the top N annotations per cluster including the percentage of cells
    """
    dict_clus_overlap = {}
    # list_clusters holds the group names as strings
    cluster_names = adata.obs[clustering].astype(str)

    for clus in list_clusters:
        size = adata[ cluster_names == clus ].shape[0]
        list_topn = adata[ cluster_names == clus ].obs.value_counts(annotation)[0:ntop]
        
        ratios = list_topn / size
        ratios = ratios[ ratios >= min_overlap_ratio]
        list_str = [ label + ' (' + str(round(ratio* 100, 2)) + '%)' for label, ratio in zip(ratios.index, ratios.values) ]
        
        if len(list_str) < ntop:
            nmissing = ntop - len(list_str)
            list_str = list_str + nmissing * ['-']
        dict_clus_overlap[clus] = list_str

    df_overlap = pd.DataFrame(dict_clus_overlap).T
    df_overlap.index.name = 'Cluster'
    df_overlap.columns = ['top ' +  str(i+1) for i in list(range(ntop)) ]

    return df_overlap
```

```{python}
from IPython.display import display, HTML

        html += '</font></h3><font color="black"><details><summary>Click to expand table</summary>'
        html += '<div style="overflow-y: scroll; overflow-x: scroll; max-height: 400px">' + df_overlap.to_html() + '</div></details></font>'
```

## <font color='green'>Requested UMAP plots</font>

```{python}
# Requested UMAP colourings: the obs columns in --umap_color_by, one figure per embedding in
# --umap_color_by_embeddings (outer loop: embeddings, inner loop: columns). The plots use a small
# in-memory AnnData holding only those columns and embeddings, so scanpy's sanitize step (strings
# to categories) never writes to the report object, which may be opened backed.
import math
from html import escape as html_escape

import anndata as ad
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import display, HTML

color_by_max_legend_categories = 50

def parse_list_param(value):
    # comma-separated -P value; quarto passes an empty value as null
    if value is None:
        return []
    items = [item.strip() for item in str(value).split(",")]
    return list(dict.fromkeys(item for item in items if item and item.lower() not in ("none", "null")))

def color_by_title(key):
    if key in ['X_umap', 'X_umap_pca']:
        name = "Before integration (PCA UMAP)"
    elif key == "X_umap_scvi":
        name = "After integration (scVI UMAP)"
    else:
        name = key.removeprefix("X_umap_") + " UMAP"

    return name

def color_by_note(text):
    display(HTML(f"<p><b>Note:</b> {text}</p>"))

def html_list(names):
    return ", ".join(html_escape(str(name)) for name in names)

color_by_cols = parse_list_param(UMAP_COLOR_BY)

if not color_by_cols:
    display(HTML("<p>No columns requested. Set <code>--umap_color_by</code> (e.g. <code>sex,diagnosis</code>) "
                 "to plot obs columns here.</p>"))
else:
    # embeddings: accept X_umap_pca or umap_pca; X_umap and X_umap_pca are the same, keep the first requested
    color_by_obsm, missing_embeddings, unusable_embeddings, seen_titles = {}, [], [], set()
    for name in parse_list_param(UMAP_COLOR_BY_EMBEDDINGS):
        key = next((k for k in (name, f"X_{name}") if k in adata.obsm), None)
        if key is None:
            missing_embeddings.append(name)
            continue
        if color_by_title(key) in seen_titles:
            continue
        coords = np.asarray(adata.obsm[key])
        if coords.ndim != 2 or coords.shape[1] < 2:
            unusable_embeddings.append(key)
            continue
        seen_titles.add(color_by_title(key))
        color_by_obsm[key] = coords

    missing_cols = [col for col in color_by_cols if col not in adata.obs.columns]
    color_by_cols = [col for col in color_by_cols if col in adata.obs.columns]

    if missing_embeddings:
        color_by_note(f"Embedding(s) not found in adata.obsm and skipped: {html_list(missing_embeddings)}. "
                      f"Available: {html_list(adata.obsm.keys())}.")
    if unusable_embeddings:
        color_by_note(f"Embedding(s) with fewer than two dimensions skipped: {html_list(unusable_embeddings)}.")
    if missing_cols:
        color_by_note(f"Column(s) not found in adata.obs and skipped: {html_list(missing_cols)}. "
                      f"Available: {html_list(adata.obs.columns)}.")
    if not color_by_obsm:
        color_by_note("No embedding to plot. Set <code>--umap_color_by_embeddings</code> "
                      "(e.g. <code>X_umap_pca,X_umap_scvi</code>).")
    if not color_by_cols:
        color_by_note("None of the requested columns is in adata.obs.")

    if color_by_obsm and color_by_cols:
        color_by_obs = adata.obs[color_by_cols].copy()
        for col in color_by_cols:
            values = color_by_obs[col]
            if isinstance(values.dtype, pd.CategoricalDtype):
                color_by_obs[col] = values.cat.remove_unused_categories()
            elif pd.api.types.is_object_dtype(values) or pd.api.types.is_string_dtype(values):
                try:
                    color_by_obs[col] = values.astype("category")
                except TypeError:
                    color_by_obs[col] = values.astype(str).astype("category")
        adata_color_by = ad.AnnData(obs=color_by_obs, obsm=color_by_obsm)

        many_categories = [col for col in color_by_cols
                           if isinstance(color_by_obs[col].dtype, pd.CategoricalDtype)
                           and len(color_by_obs[col].cat.categories) > color_by_max_legend_categories]
        if many_categories:
            color_by_note(f"Legend hidden for column(s) with more than {color_by_max_legend_categories} "
                          f"categories: {html_list(many_categories)}.")

        ncols = min(3, len(color_by_cols))
        nrows = math.ceil(len(color_by_cols) / ncols)
        failed_panels = []

        for key in color_by_obsm:
            display(HTML(f"<h3>{html_escape(color_by_title(key))}</h3>"))
            fig, axs = plt.subplots(nrows, ncols, figsize=(ncols * 6, nrows * 5), squeeze=False,
                                    layout="constrained")
            panels = axs.ravel()

            for ax, col in zip(panels, color_by_cols):
                legend_kwargs = {"legend_loc": None} if col in many_categories else {}
                try:
                    sc.pl.embedding(adata_color_by, basis=key, color=col, ax=ax, show=False, title=col,
                                    **legend_kwargs)
                except Exception as err:
                    ax.clear()
                    ax.set_axis_off()
                    failed_panels.append(f"{html_escape(str(col))} on {html_escape(key)} ({html_escape(str(err))})")

            for ax in panels[len(color_by_cols):]:
                ax.set_axis_off()

            plt.show()
            plt.close(fig)

        if failed_panels:
            color_by_note(f"Could not plot: {'; '.join(failed_panels)}.")
```

```{python}
from IPython.display import display, HTML

marker_results = adata.uns['rank_genes_groups']
# presto results (Wilcoxon test, AUC, p-values) have 'auc', COSG results 'cosg_scores'; either or both
has_presto = 'auc' in marker_results
has_cosg = 'cosg_scores' in marker_results
marker_ranked_by = marker_results['params'].get('ranked_by', 'auc' if has_presto else 'cosg')

# used in the column legend above the marker tables
cosg_definition = (
    "cosine similarity between the expression of a gene and membership of the cluster, penalised when the "
    "gene is also similar to other clusters; higher means more specific to the cluster"
)
if marker_ranked_by == 'cosg':
    marker_method_text = (
        "Marker genes per cluster are found with COSG, comparing the cells of a cluster against all other cells, "
        "and ranked by the COSG score; ties are ordered by log2FC, then by pct in."
    )
    if has_presto:
        marker_method_text += " The Wilcoxon rank-sum test and AUC (presto) of the same comparison are shown too."
else:
    marker_method_text = (
        "Marker genes per cluster are found with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test and the AUC (presto), comparing the "
        "cells of a cluster against all other cells, and ranked by AUC; ties are ordered by adj. p, then by log2FC"
        + (", then by the COSG score." if has_cosg else ".")
    )
    if has_cosg:
        marker_method_text += " COSG scores of the same comparison are shown too."

display(HTML(f"<p>{marker_method_text}</p>"))
```

```{python}
# helper function for creating HTML table
import pandas as pd

def create_search_table_html(df: pd.DataFrame, search_text: str, 
                             sbox_name: str, table_name: str, ntop: int=100,
                             lookupFunction: str="searchTable") -> str:
    """
    Creates HTML string for searchable table

    Parameters
    ----------
    df: pd.DataFrame
        Pandas DataFrame to be turned into searchable table
    search_text: str
        Text that will be displayed in search box before typing
    sbox_name: str
        Unique searchbox ID that will be assigned
    table_name: str
        Unique table ID that will be assigned
    ntop: int
        Limit the number of rows to this number to avoid giant HTMLs
    lookupFunction: str
        JavaScript function for text search, has to be defined beforehand. 

    Returns
    -------
    str
        HTML table string trhat can be disaplyed with IPython.display.HTML
    """

    # input search box
    table_html = "<input type='text' id='" + box_name + "' onkeyup=\"" + lookupFunction  + "('" + box_name + "', '" + table_name + "')\" "
    table_html += "placeholder='"  + search_text + "'"
    table_html += "style='width: 100%; max-width: 300px; padding: 10px; margin-top: 12px; font-family: sans-serif; border: 1px solid #D1D5DB; border-radius: 4px;'>"

    # table
    table_html += "<div id=" + table_name + " style='overflow-y: scroll; max-height: 400px'>" + df.to_html(index=False, max_rows=ntop) + "</div>"

    return table_html
```

```{python}
from IPython.display import display, HTML

# column legend, one bullet per table column in the order of marker_table()
marker_legend = []
if has_presto:
    marker_legend.append(('AUC', 'auc', "probability that a random cell of the cluster expresses the gene more "
                          "highly than a random other cell; 0.5 means no difference, 1 a perfect marker"))
if has_cosg:
    marker_legend.append(('COSG score', 'cosg', cosg_definition))
marker_legend += [
    ('log2FC', None, "log2 fold change of the cluster over all other cells: the mean log-normalised expression "
     "of each, converted back with expm1, as in scanpy"),
    ('pct in', None, "percentage of cells of the cluster in which the gene is detected"),
    ('pct out', None, "percentage of all other cells in which the gene is detected"),
]
if has_presto:
    marker_legend += [
        ('p', None, "p-value of the Wilcoxon rank-sum test"),
        ('adj. p', None, "Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value of the Wilcoxon rank-sum test"),
    ]

display(HTML(
    f"<p>Tables show the top {ntop} genes per cluster, in ranking order. Columns:</p><ul>"
    + "".join(f"<li><b>{name}</b>{' (ranking)' if key == marker_ranked_by else ''}: {text}</li>"
              for name, key, text in marker_legend)
    + "</ul>"
))
```

```{python}
# filter panel for all marker tables; inputs start empty, an empty input applies no filter
from IPython.display import display, HTML

marker_filter_js = """
<script>
function markerCellValue(text) {
    let t = text.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (t === 'inf') return Infinity;
    if (t === '-inf') return -Infinity;
    return parseFloat(t);
}

function markerFilterValues() {
    let filters = [];
    document.querySelectorAll('.marker-filter').forEach(input => {
        let value = parseFloat(input.value);
        if (!Number.isNaN(value)) {
            filters.push({col: input.dataset.col, op: input.dataset.op, value: value});
        }
    });
    return filters;
}

function filterMarkerTable(block, filters) {
    let headers = Array.from(block.querySelectorAll('thead th')).map(th => th.textContent.trim());
    let search = document.getElementById(block.dataset.search).value.toLowerCase();
    let rows = block.querySelectorAll('tbody tr');
    let shown = 0;
    rows.forEach(row => {
        let keep = row.textContent.toLowerCase().includes(search);
        filters.forEach(f => {
            let idx = headers.indexOf(f.col);
            if (!keep || idx < 0) return;
            let x = markerCellValue(row.cells[idx].textContent);
            keep = !Number.isNaN(x) && (f.op === 'min' ? x >= f.value : x <= f.value);
        });
        row.style.display = keep ? '' : 'none';
        if (keep) shown++;
    });
    document.getElementById(block.dataset.count).textContent = shown + ' of ' + rows.length + ' genes shown';
}

function applyMarkerFilters() {
    let filters = markerFilterValues();
    document.querySelectorAll('.marker-table').forEach(block => filterMarkerTable(block, filters));
}

function markerSearchTable(inputId, containerId) {
    filterMarkerTable(document.getElementById(containerId).closest('.marker-table'), markerFilterValues());
}

function resetMarkerFilters() {
    document.querySelectorAll('.marker-filter').forEach(input => { input.value = ''; });
    applyMarkerFilters();
}
</script>
"""

marker_filter_style = ("width: 110px; padding: 6px; margin-top: 4px; font-family: sans-serif; "
                       "border: 1px solid #D1D5DB; border-radius: 4px;")

def marker_filter_input(input_id: str, label: str, column: str, op: str) -> str:
    """Numeric filter input; data-col is the table header it applies to, data-op 'min' or 'max'."""
    return ("<label style='display: flex; flex-direction: column; font-size: 0.85em; font-family: sans-serif;'>"
            + label
            + f"<input type='number' step='any' id='{input_id}' class='marker-filter' data-col='{column}' "
            + f"data-op='{op}' placeholder='no filter' oninput='applyMarkerFilters()' style='{marker_filter_style}'>"
            + "</label>")

# one input per table column that exists (AUC, p and adj. p only with presto; COSG score only with COSG)
marker_filters = []
if has_presto:
    marker_filters.append(('markerFilterMinAuc', 'min AUC', 'AUC', 'min'))
if has_cosg:
    marker_filters.append(('markerFilterMinCosg', 'min COSG score', 'COSG score', 'min'))
marker_filters.append(('markerFilterMinLogfc', 'min log2FC', 'log2FC', 'min'))
if has_presto:
    marker_filters += [
        ('markerFilterMaxP', 'max p', 'p', 'max'),
        ('markerFilterMaxPadj', 'max adj. p', 'adj. p', 'max'),
    ]
marker_filters += [
    ('markerFilterMinPctIn', 'min pct in (%)', 'pct in', 'min'),
    ('markerFilterMaxPctOut', 'max pct out (%)', 'pct out', 'max'),
]

# the pipeline parameters that filter the exported marker JSON for these results
marker_export_params = ((["--markers_min_auc"] if has_presto else [])
                        + ["--markers_min_logfc", "--markers_pct_nz"]
                        + (["--markers_min_cosg_score"] if has_cosg else []))

marker_filter_panel = (
    "<div id='markerFilterPanel' style='display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px; align-items: flex-end; "
    "margin: 12px 0;'>"
    + "".join(marker_filter_input(*f) for f in marker_filters)
    + "<button type='button' id='markerFilterReset' onclick='resetMarkerFilters()' "
    "style='padding: 6px 14px; font-family: sans-serif; border: 1px solid #D1D5DB; border-radius: 4px; "
    "background: #F9FAFB; cursor: pointer;'>Reset</button>"
    "</div>"
)

display(HTML(
    marker_filter_js
    + "<ul>"
    + f"<li>The filters below act on the genes shown (the top {ntop} per cluster) in all cluster tables, "
    "together with each table's gene search.</li>"
    + "<li>An empty field applies no filter.</li>"
    + "<li>The exported marker JSON is filtered with the pipeline parameters "
    + ", ".join(marker_export_params[:-1]) + " and " + marker_export_params[-1] + " instead.</li>"
    + "</ul>"
    + marker_filter_panel
))
```

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import display, HTML

def marker_table(results: dict, group: str, ntop: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Top ntop genes of one cluster from the uns fields, in the stored ranking order."""
    names = np.asarray(results['names'][group]).astype(str)[:ntop]
    table = pd.DataFrame({'gene': names})
    if 'auc' in results:
        table['AUC'] = np.asarray(results['auc'][group][:ntop], dtype=float).round(3)
    if 'cosg_scores' in results:
        table['COSG score'] = np.asarray(results['cosg_scores'][group][:ntop], dtype=float).round(3)
    table['log2FC'] = np.asarray(results['logfoldchanges'][group][:ntop], dtype=float).round(2)
    table['pct in'] = (100 * results['pts'][group].reindex(names).to_numpy(dtype=float)).round(1)
    table['pct out'] = (100 * results['pts_rest'][group].reindex(names).to_numpy(dtype=float)).round(1)
    if 'pvals' in results:
        table['p'] = [f"{p:.2e}" for p in np.asarray(results['pvals'][group][:ntop], dtype=float)]
        table['adj. p'] = [f"{p:.2e}" for p in np.asarray(results['pvals_adj'][group][:ntop], dtype=float)]
    return table

tableid = 0
for clus in list_clusters:

    box_name = 'sboxDiff' + str(tableid)
    table_name = 'tableDiff' + str(tableid)
    count_name = 'countDiff' + str(tableid)
    text = "Search gene..."

    df_markers = marker_table(marker_results, clus, ntop)
    html = create_search_table_html(df_markers, text, box_name, table_name, ntop,
                                    lookupFunction="markerSearchTable")
    count_html = (f"<span id='{count_name}' style='margin-left: 12px; font-size: 0.6em; color: #6B7280;'>"
                  f"{len(df_markers)} of {len(df_markers)} genes shown</span>")
    display(HTML("<h3><font color='green'>Differential genes cluster" + clus +  "</font>" + count_html + "</h3>"
                 + f"<details><div class='marker-table' data-search='{box_name}' data-count='{count_name}'>"
                 + html + "</div></details>"))
    
    tableid += 1
```

## <font color='green'>Cell-cell interaction</font>

LIANA+ consensus ligand-receptor interactions. LIANA+ uses ranking and aggregating to compute a `magnitude rank`. A lower `magnitude rank` indicates that an interaction is more likely to occur.

Following methods are currently implemented in the LIANA+ framework:

```{python}
import liana as li

li.mt.show_methods()
```

```{python}
# create images
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import math

ntop_liana_dotplot = 20

paths_images = {}
clusters_without_interactions = []
dotplot_failures = []

if 'liana_res' in adata.uns:
    liana_res = adata.uns['liana_res']

    for clus in list_clusters:
        # li.pl.dotplot filters by source first and then raises for any requested target
        # that is missing from the remaining rows, so the targets must be taken per source.
        # LIANA+ also skips clusters with too few cells (min_cells=5).
        res_clus = liana_res[liana_res['source'].astype(str) == clus]
        clus_targets = set(res_clus['target'].astype(str))
        target_labels = [c for c in list_clusters if c in clus_targets]

        if res_clus.empty or not target_labels:
            clusters_without_interactions.append(clus)
            continue

        path_img = f"./dotplot_test_clus{clus}.png"

        try:
            fig = li.pl.dotplot(adata = adata,
                  colour='magnitude_rank',
                  size='specificity_rank',
                  inverse_size=True,
                  inverse_colour=True,
                  source_labels=[clus],
                  target_labels=target_labels,
                  top_n=ntop_liana_dotplot,
                  orderby='magnitude_rank',
                  orderby_ascending=True,
                  return_fig=True)

            fig.save(path_img, bbox_inches='tight')
        except ValueError as err:
            # one cluster must never stop the report; it is reported in the HTML output
            dotplot_failures.append((clus, str(err)))
            continue

        paths_images[clus] = path_img
```

```{python}
# HTML output
from IPython.display import display, HTML
from html import escape
import base64

if 'liana_res' in adata.uns:
    df_liana = adata.uns['liana_res'].copy()

    if clusters_without_interactions:
        display(HTML(
            f"<p>No LIANA+ interactions with cluster(s) {', '.join(clusters_without_interactions)} as source. "
            "LIANA+ skips clusters with fewer than 5 cells, and a cluster can have no interactions that pass its filters.</p>"
        ))

    failure_messages = dict(dotplot_failures)

    tableid = 0

    for clus in list_clusters:
        if clus not in paths_images and clus not in failure_messages:
            continue

        image_html = f'<h3><font color="green">Interactions cluster {clus}</font></h3>'

        # dotplot
        if clus in paths_images:
            with open(paths_images[clus], "rb") as f_plot:
                image_string = base64.b64encode(f_plot.read()).decode("utf-8")
            image_html += '<details><summary>Click to expand dotplot</summary>'
            image_html += f'<figure><img alt="liana image" src="data:image/png;base64,{image_string}" />'
            image_html += f'<figcaption>Shown are the top {ntop_liana_dotplot} interactions between cluster {clus} and the other clusters. '
            image_html += 'The color gradient and dot size indicate the -log10 <i>magnitude rank</i> and <i>specificity rank</i>, respectively. Higher values are better.</figcaption></figure></details>'
        else:
            image_html += f'<p>Dotplot for cluster {clus} could not be drawn: {escape(failure_messages[clus])}</p>'

        # table
        df_liana_clus = df_liana[ df_liana['source'].astype(str) == clus]

        if not df_liana_clus.empty:
            box_name = 'sboxLiana' + str(tableid)
            table_name = 'tableLiana' + str(tableid)
            text = "Search gene..."

            html = create_search_table_html(df_liana_clus, text, box_name, table_name, ntop)
            image_html += '<font color="black"><details><summary>Click to expand table</summary>'
            image_html += html
            image_html += f"<p>Results in tables are limited to the top {ntop} interactions.</p></details></font>"

            tableid += 1

        display(HTML(image_html))
```
